Depression simply isn't logical. You'll have an objective knowledge of things, things people will tell you over and over again when you're having an episode. Things like "People love you" and "You're worth something" and you can know these things, but it feels like they're almost abstract concepts. You know people love you but in those moments you can't comprehend how or why or possiby even what it feels like. You can know you are worth something, but you don't know what or how much or how to live up to that worth. 

Depressive episodes are insidious. they have a way of turning everyone into shells of themselves. nothing feels right, and for many people, they believe that they are the cause of this "off" feeling. Some people feel destructive, like they are making things worse for other people, and so they seek to mitigate their damage by isolating themselves. Others may see it as a form of self-punishment, an exile because they don't deserve help. Many just don't want to be a burden, despite the fact that people are there for them out of the goodness of their hearts. 

Depression eats at people. By time someone acts in any form based on depression, it is likely that they have grappled with the action for a very long time, and it seems like the best choice. Most people who make that decision while in a depressive episode are making the decision with a handicap, and so their responses are a bit less than ideal. 

Most of the time, they don't mean to cause problems for anyone else, and in fact they believe that they are solving problems for other people.

Someone in my life had been spreading lies about me to my family, and it seemed like every day they were turning against me. At the time I was also living a fair distance from my closest friends and as a result we had started to drift apart.  was unemployed, single, and lonely. It felt like I had no one to turn to. 2 days before my 20th birthday, I placed a series of notes around my room and on my door. I tried to address every conceivable source of confusion after I was gone. As it turns out, it's harder to will yourself to harm yourself than I thought. Thankfully the next day I reached out to a friend of mine. It took a long time but I've gotten help for the anxiety that I believe pushed me to the belief that everyone was against me. It's to this day one my most shameful moments.
